title: Never expecting records to last; turning down television
summary: She never thought her early records would bring fame or that people would listen in 1976, and has turned down television offers.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Do you remember making those first records, what it was like? What did you think of -- how did you look on records? You didn't think of that records as something that was going to bring you a lot of money fame.

No. And I tell you one thing, I didn't look on it, and I didn't think in life that I'd ever be doing what I'm doing. No. You'll excuse me if I just fill up a little here. I never thought, I never thought -- I always strove to make good. That was my ambition, to go high. I've always wanted to go high. But I never thought this would -- that I'd get this. Funny, you see.

But when I made my records, I made the record and I thought, for the time being it's something wonderful. And I hope I can continue going. But I didn't know I would be. I knew I wanted to go at it.
You never thought that in 1976 people would still be listening?
I never thought. I never thought, no. And I get offers to do television and to do things now. I've had so many offers for television. And you know that I've turned several of them down.
Yeah. So when I made "How Come, Sweet Daddy, How Come," -- I told you that was for Pace and Handy?
